quiz.q: What are the four parts of a candle?
quiz.explain: A candle needs wax to burn, a wick to light, scent to smell and a container to hold it.

quiz.q: What does the wick do?
options: Burns and melts the wax so the candle gives light and scent
quiz.explain: The wick is the string that burns and melts wax around it.

quiz.q: Why use a thermometer when melting wax?
options: So the wax never gets hot enough to catch fire

days.title: Cooling and Setting
days.goal: Let candles cool slowly so they set smooth and even.

video.title: How to Make Soy Candles the Easy Way

steps: Leave candles to cool at room temperature, not in a fridge.
Do not move them while they set.
Wait at least 24 hours before you burn a new candle.

options: The melt pool is small and the candle tunnels

quiz.q: What happens if the wick is too big?
options: The flame is big and the candle smokes
quiz.explain: A big wick makes a tall smoky flame and burns the candle too fast.

quiz.q: How do you centre a wick?
options: Stick it to the bottom and hold it straight with a wick bar
quiz.explain: A wick sticker and a bar across the jar keep the wick centred.
